skill: Apply explicitly specified elementary row operations to an ordinary 3-by-3 coefficient matrix and select the resulting matrix.
reasoning_steps: Read the operation type and indexed row roles.
Swap exactly the specified rows, multiply every entry of the specified row by a nonzero scalar, or add the indicated multiple of the source row to the destination row.
For two operations use the intermediate matrix in the listed order. Preserve all unassigned rows.
Compare the full resulting matrix against a five-choice math radio bank.
response_contract: All 11 bank questions use one math radio field keyed selection, five complete matrix options, one correct choice. Canonical example has a solution but no captured answer bank.
difficulty: easy: single swaps or reciprocal scaling with integral result; moderate: one row addition; hard: two row additions, either distinct destinations or repeated destination. Requested easy should retain easy workload.
invariants: Ordinary coefficient matrix, no augmentation bar.
Specified operations, not inverse identification, elimination planning, solving systems, or entry targeting.
Row replacement uses the old/current source row and updates all columns; unchanged rows remain equal.
Nonzero scaling and distinct source/destination row indices.
permitted_variations: Vary signed integer matrix entries conservatively with comparable arithmetic.
Swap any pair of distinct rows; vary scaling target across all rows and nonzero reciprocal scalar with divisible entries.
Vary addition source and destination rows, scalar sign/magnitude, and whether entries cancel: a zero in the first column is incidental, not a required answer role.
Vary hard ordered row roles within the demonstrated two-addition workload.
Vary matrix name, complete plausible distractors, and correct-choice position; none should predict correctness.
